objects.original: Boumal: a Riemannian submanifold M of Euclidean E, smooth f:M→ℝ, any smooth neighborhood extension f̄, tangent spaces T_xM, and their orthogonal projectors. The candidate intentionally selects their affine restriction mechanism.
objects.reconstructed: Complete real inner-product E, complete linear subspace K with inherited inner product, ambient f:E→ℝ, shift a, gradient vector g, u∈K, and F_a(v)=f(a+v).
objects.evidence: PDF58–60/printed42–44, Definition3.58, equations3.36–3.38 and Proposition3.61 versus production binders and literal restriction. M=a+K gives the affine geometric specialization; no nonlinear manifold objects are formalized.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional Euclidean ambient space; f is defined on a smooth submanifold and f̄ on a neighborhood; the gradient at x lies in T_xM.
domains.reconstructed: Real Hilbert E and complete K; f is globally typed on E, restriction globally typed on K, evaluation at a+u; projected gradient is a K subtype vector.
domains.evidence: The theorem uses [CompleteSpace E], (K:Submodule ℝ E), [CompleteSpace K], and K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g. Infinite-dimensional completeness extends the ambient setting; a fixed affine subspace and globally typed ambient function restrict the geometric representation. Neither is full-source equivalence.

quantifiers.original: For every smooth manifold objective and every x∈M, the projection identity holds for any smooth neighborhood extension; the gradient is identified by pairings with every v∈T_xM.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admitted E,K,f,a,g,u, HasGradientAt f g (a+u) implies the restriction gradient assertion at u; equality of functionals is proved for every v∈K.
quantifiers.evidence: All production parameters are arbitrary and the hf implication is pointwise. hdual uses ext v. The theorem does not quantify over smooth extensions of one fixed manifold function and does not establish their independence.

assumptions.original: Smooth f and smooth neighborhood extension; induced Riemannian metric on finite-dimensional embedded M. Finite-dimensional inner-product spaces and tangent subspaces are complete.
assumptions.reconstructed: Explicit real inner-product structure and completeness for E and K; hf is genuine HasGradientAt at a+u. The K metric is inherited. No derivative or gradient of the restriction is assumed.
assumptions.evidence: Pointwise HasGradientAt supplies the ambient Fréchet derivative for hcomp; hchart constructs the restriction parameterization derivative. Source smoothness entails pointwise differentiability in the affine specialization; the local theorem has weaker regularity and explicit Hilbert completeness.

conclusion.original: The Riemannian gradient field satisfies grad_M f(x)=Proj_x(grad_E f̄(x)) for all x, with tangent-space metric and any extension.
conclusion.reconstructed: HasGradientAt (fun v:K=>f(a+(v:E))) (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g) u. The projected vector represents the genuine restriction derivative at u.
conclusion.evidence: The pointwise affine conclusion matches the projection pairing mechanism. It does not prove a manifold gradient-field construction, nonlinear differential identification, smooth-field regularity, or general neighborhood-extension independence. The lesson explicitly labels this boundary.

scopes.original: The smooth embedded-manifold projection recipe with induced metric, summarizing equations3.36–3.38 in Proposition3.61.
scopes.reconstructed: A single arbitrary affine point and inherited subspace metric; a is a point translation, g and P_K g are vectors. The binding supports only affine-gradient with role prerequisite.
scopes.evidence: The production module docstring, lesson assumptions and packet binding all restrict scope to a canonical prerequisite. The chapter_reader separately leaves nonlinear tangent/differential, neighborhood-extension semantics and smooth-field work open.

constant_dependencies.original: No numerical constants or rate parameters; projector and gradient depend on ambient/induced inner products and the base point tangent space.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No numerical constants; the projector depends on K and its inherited inner product; the derivative is evaluated at a+u and shift a has zero derivative.
constant_dependencies.evidence: All three formulas preserve this absence of numerical constants. Source base-point-varying tangent spaces specialize to the fixed K of an affine space; no dimension, norm or smoothness constants are introduced.

deltas.description: Complete Hilbert E with complete K is broader than finite Euclidean ambient geometry, while the fixed affine restriction is narrower than arbitrary embedded M. Accept the prerequisite binding only; reject interpreting this as Proposition3.61 completion.

The theorem assumes genuine ambient gradient existence at one point rather than source smoothness of a manifold function and neighborhood extension. It proves the restriction derivative; it never assumes that derivative as an extra public premise.

Nonlinear tangent/differential identification, neighborhood-extension semantics and smoothness of the manifold gradient field remain open. The candidate publication and chapter map retain all three boundaries.

verdict_explanation: The complete source proposition and the affine Lean theorem have intentionally different domains and scopes. Their affine projection mechanism agrees. Accepted as an explicitly narrower geometric prerequisite with generalized ambient/pointwise assumptions, never as a source-equivalent manifold theorem.

source_review.evidence: Independently read pinned PDF58–60/printed42–44. Equations3.36–3.38 derive projection from equality of tangent pairings and inherited metric. The actual Lean proof derives its differential by the affine chart and chain rule, then equates Riesz functionals through orthogonal projection. No source-independent premise replaces a proof ingredient.

exposition_review.claim_and_formula: The lesson states the exact Hilbert-space affine restriction with a genuine ambient gradient, complete K and inherited metric. The formula treats P_Kg as a direction in K, not an affine point.
